chapter_theme: Songs at Virinchipuram (விரிஞ்சிபுரம்), also named Thiruvirinchai and Karapuram in the songs: the poet confesses the courtesans who play their lovers against each other and take his wealth, his neglect of rites, austerity and giving, and the five elements he cannot cast off; he asks for the feet, for love that melts, and for the formless state, and the praise names Murugan as teacher of Siva and as the Tamil child who impaled the Jains.
structure_note: Courtesan and desire songs (668, 669, 671); a song on the feet beyond the sects (670); and a song on the formless state and Murugan as first guru (672). Songs 668, 669 and 671 end at Karapuram (கரபுரம்), 670 and 672 at Thiruvirinchai.

668.reading: The poet describes women who keep one man on the bed in a small house, set another circling at their door, send a third rushing about the street, set lovers against each other until they draw knives and fight in the room, and think it all fitting so long as they make a living; deluded by them he abandoned the path of austerity, chariyai, kiriyai and tapas, threw away his wealth and wandered scorned, and asks grace that his sorrows end, good qualities come and he think always with love of the golden feet. The praise names the vel that ended the cruel demons who imprisoned the ascetic sages (புலவர்), Valli of cuckoo speech, and Murugan who impaled the shaven-headed Jains, at Karapuram of areca, plantain and cane.
668.nuance: The opening is a sharp comic sketch of a courtesan managing four men at once (ஒருவரை ... ஒருவரை ... ஒருவரை), her motive given as உயிர்பிழைப்பது, earning a living. The loss is named in Saiva terms: சரியையில் கிரியையில் தவமும் அற்று. கழுவின் உச்சியில் வைத்திடுவோனே identifies Murugan with Sambandar at Madurai. Who the imprisoned புலவர் are (gods or poets) is not clear.

669.reading: The poet pictures lovemaking on the bed, the hair loosened, eyes closing, cooing voice, sweat on the face, prattle and anklets on both feet, and asks Murugan to think of ruling even the sinner whose mind will not let go of that desire. The praise names Murugan the son of Siva whose bow is a mountain, the lord riding the peacock, who came to Madurai so the Jain thieves went to the stake, the nephew of Vishnu whose lotus foot made the stone Ahalya a woman again, at Karapuri where long valai fish leap at the areca palms.
669.nuance: பதகனையும் ஆள நினைவாயே: the plea asks only to be thought of, the 'even' (உம்) marking the poet as least worthy. The Madurai impalement again gives Murugan Sambandar's deed. Ahalya's release by Rama's foot is told as Vishnu's.

670.reading: The poet asks for the lotus feet with tinkling anklets that are seen in solitude, beyond the five elements, the thinking heart and the life, which the Veda names as radiant, partless and beyond, and which the disputants of the five sects, roaring like the sea, do not know. The praise tells of the sea boiling and crying out, the way opened in the sky, Sura and his army killed so Indra and the gods could return home, and the vel that shattered the high peak, and names Murugan the son of Chandrasekhara at Thiruvirinchai, worshipped by the kings of every quarter and by four-faced Brahma.
670.nuance: சமய பஞ்ச பாதகர் அறியாத: the feet are what the sect-disputants cannot know; the knowing is தனிமை கண்ட, in solitude. The run நிகழ்தரும் ப்ரபாகர நிரவயம் பராபர நிருப reads as Sanskrit names of the Absolute but its division is uncertain. திசைமுகன் பராவிய திருவிரிஞ்சை: the town's name is tied to Brahma (விரிஞ்சன்).

671.reading: The poet asks whether, instead of holding in his mind with love Murugan's golden hands, faces, pearl-hung chest, radiance, flower feet, cock and peacock, and instead of giving in dharma even a handful of food to those who come in real hunger, he must wander deluded, embracing women who speak sweet friendship as if old acquaintances, give amorous play and snatch his wealth. The praise names the vel that cut down the dark demons until the vultures were full, Murugan who made Brahma, Vishnu, Varuna, Agni, Yama and Indra stand firm, the noble one who gave grace before Siva, the dancer with the poisoned throat, tiger skin and serpents, and the lord at Karapuram who daily tells the meaning of the Vedas to the sages.
671.nuance: The neglect confessed is twofold: contemplation of the Lord's form and feeding the hungry (பசியில் வருமவர்க்கு அசனம் ஒருபிடி படையாதே). உரிய பொருள் பறித்திடுமானார: the women take what rightly belongs to him. உத்தமவேள் may mean Murugan taught before Siva the dancer, as elsewhere in the book.

672.reading: The poet confesses that he does not know how to cast off the five elements as filth not his own, lives in delusion, and has not come by the proper way; he asks that, melting with love and thinking of Murugan daily, he reach the stage that has no form and does not even speak of 'the world', and be given the paired high feet. The praise names Murugan the first guru, whom Siva, the Lord whom Vishnu and Brahma could not find, bowed to and asked 'grant it', and to whom Murugan showed 'this is the meaning'; the vel that split the mountain; and Thiruvirinchai, whose streets resound with the Veda.
672.nuance: உலகம் என்று பேச அறியாத உருவம் ஒன்றிலாத பருவம்: the goal is a state without form in which the world is not even named. The myth of Murugan teaching Siva is told with Siva bowing at his feet (அடிபணிந்து பேசி), though Om is not named. மலம் இது என்று போட: the elements of the body are to be thrown off as impurity.

links.note: Both make a single handful of food for the hungry the measure of dharma; 671 confesses the poet did not give even that one handful (ஒருபிடி) while he spent himself on courtesans, where Tirumular sets it as what anyone can do.

The faithful wife of the Naladiyar wonders how women who embrace many men's chests for gain (பொருள்நசையால் பன்மார்பு சேர்ந்தொழுகுவார்) manage it every day. The song shows exactly how: one man on the bed, one circling the door, one rushing in the street, set against each other (ஒருவரை ... ஒருவரை ... ஒருவரை), all thought fitting as a living (உயிர்பிழைப்பது). The song answers the wife's question with the courtesan's method and motive.

The poet confesses a mind that will not let go of desire (ஆசை விட மனம் ஒவ்வாத பதகன்) and asks Murugan to think of ruling even him. Tirumular says that even if those who praise Hara come wrapped in maya (மாயகம் சூழ்ந்து வரவல்லராகிலும்), the Lord becomes one with them. Both hold that delusion still clinging is no bar to being taken by the Lord; the Tirumanthiram verse is obscure in its second line, so the agreement rests on its third and fourth.

The poet asks for the feet that the disputants of the five sects, roaring like the sea, do not know (சமய பஞ்ச பாதகர் அறியாத), feet seen in solitude (தனிமை கண்ட). Tirumular says the six sects standing in the assembly do not see the God standing in the body (ஆயத்துள் நின்ற ... காயத்துள் நின்ற கடவுளைக் காண்கிலர்). Both set the sects' public contest against an inward, solitary seeing.

Here the poet asks to cast off the five elements as impurity (மலமிது என்று போட) and reach a formless stage that does not even speak of 'the world' (உலகமென்று பேச அறியாத உருவமொன்றிலாத பருவம்). At Nimbapuram he asks for the one release that knows neither the five elements nor the four inner faculties nor night and day, with no end, middle or beginning (அந்தநடு ஆதி ஒன்றுமிலதான). The two songs define the goal the same way, by negation of the elements and of form.

source_issues: Song 670: one corrupt character in புண்ட஡ணகம (line 8), probably புண்டரீகம (஡ண for ரீ).
Songs 668, 669 and 671 end at Karapuram (கரபுரம், கரபுரி), not Virinchipuram; 670 and 672 name Thiruvirinchai. Karapuram may be another name of the shrine.
